selected_evidence.requirement: Rotate daily and retain seven compressed rotations
selected_evidence.summary: The installed policy specifies daily, rotate 7, and compress. A forced rotation produced a valid app.log.1.gz archive, and the system timer declares OnCalendar=daily.

selected_evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
selected_evidence.summary: A writer held app.log open during rotation. copytruncate preserved the inode and open descriptor, and the writer's post-rotation record appeared in the active log.

selected_evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software
selected_evidence.summary: Before and after work, the node remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64; the existing release-native logrotate-3.22.0-4.el10 package was used.

Baseline boot ID f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c and healthy policy/data were captured; the safe reboot was acknowledged; recovered boot ID changed to 40a1d9c9-34b7-40b3-a998-2330cacde6c3; system state, timer, configuration, active log writes, and compressed archive were healthy afterward.

cat > "$tmp_cfg" <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
/var/log/inventory/app.log {
    daily
    rotate 7
    compress
    missingok
    notifempty
    copytruncate
}
ANTRIEB_EOF
chown root:root "$tmp_cfg"
chmod 0644 "$tmp_cfg"
mv -f "$tmp_cfg" /etc/logrotate.d/inventory
trap - EXIT HUP INT TERM
restorecon /etc/logrotate.d/inventory 2>/dev/null || true
logrotate -d /etc/logrotate.conf 2>&1 | sed -n '/reading config file inventory/,/reading config file/p'
printf 'INSTALLED\n'
